newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWF cuts Australian barley forecast to 6.27 MT.
newsitem.headline: AWF cuts Australian barley forecast to 6.27 MT.

text.p: Australian Wheat Forecasters Pty Ltd (AWF) slashed its second forecast of the 1997/98 Australian barley crop by 470,000 tonnes after cutting its area estimate by 130,000 hectares.
The private forecaster put its latest crop forecast at 6.27 million tonnes, down from 6.74 million a month ago, against 6.22 million in 1996/97, and its area estimate at 3.46 million hectares.
AWF said a series of good but patchy rains throughout southern Australia encouraged growers to plant crops other than barley which do well when sown early in the season.
"The opportunity has been presented to sow more of these early crops, and it will be at some penalty to the Australian barley area," AWF said.
These crops include wheat, for which spot and forward prices are edging higher, canola and chickpeas, AWF said.
However, if the early May rains are not followed up with further rainfalls to fill in the gaps, then barley would become a more attractive cropping option, AWF said.
But this would not occur until late June or July.
AWF said there has been some scattered rain through Queensland but none of it has been used for planting barley.
Similarly, the rain that has fallen in New South Wales has been used to plant wheat, canola or lupins.
Other crops are preferred to barley in both Victoria and South Australia at this time.
Western Australian barley hectares were hampered by a late start in the south for any grain last year.
The 1997 season, so far, indicates more barley will be sown in Western Australia although most will be sown in June.
The proportion of Australian barley classified as malting category is expected to be lower than last year, AWF said.
